channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: International Project on Tick-Borne Diseases Concludes in Kyrgyzstan
item.description: An international project studying the spread of dangerous viral and bacterial diseases transmitted by ticks in Kyrgyzstan has concluded. Biological samples were collected from ticks, livestock, and wild animals. The research focused on identifying areas where tick-borne disease vectors are present to aid in future prevention efforts.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan's Banks Operating Normally Amidst Cyberattack Rumors
item.description: All commercial banks in Kyrgyzstan are functioning normally, providing full services despite rumors of a large-scale cyberattack on November 17. The National Bank of the Kyrgyz Republic (NBKR) stated that reports of widespread internet, communication, and banking system failures are unconfirmed and advised checking official sources.

item.title: Kazakhstan's 'Damu' Fund Explains 30% Top Management Salary Increase
item.description: The chairman of Kazakhstan's 'Damu' Entrepreneurship Development Fund, Farhat Sarsekeyev, explained a 30% increase in top management salaries, attributing it to work results, new program launches, and inflation. The fund supported approximately 13,000 projects totaling 2.2 trillion tenge in 2025 and introduced new initiatives like mobile front-offices for entrepreneurs. The board and shareholders approved the salary adjustments.

item.title: Tashkent District Denies Reports of Mahallah Chairman's Detention
item.description: The Yashnabad district administration in Tashkent has refuted information about the detention of a mahallah chairman, previously reported by the Ministry of Internal Affairs. The administration stated that no criminal case was initiated and the mahallah head continues to perform his duties. An investigation found that the premises in question were not state property and no signs of a crime were confirmed.

item.title: Mongolian President Announces Intent to Resign Amid Corruption Allegations
item.description: Mongolia's President Khurelsukh Ukhnaa has announced his intention to resign early following corruption allegations by the parliamentary opposition. The Democratic Party claims the president and other officials benefited financially from a state railway project. The president denies the accusations and seeks an objective investigation.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Emergency Situations Minister Explains Fatal Accident in Ala-Archa National Park
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's Emergency Situations Minister Kanatbek Chynybaev reported to parliament on a fatal incident in Ala-Archa National Park where a teenager died. The minister detailed the rescue operation, noting challenges faced by rescuers due to other ongoing operations and difficult terrain. He stated he does not evade responsibility.

item.title: Kazakhstan's Electricity Prices Rise for Fourth Consecutive Month in October
item.description: Electricity prices in Kazakhstan increased by an average of 3.4% in October compared to September, marking the fourth consecutive month of rising costs. Over the year, prices have climbed 7.9%. The increase was observed in five regions, including Almaty and Almaty region, with new tariffs in effect since September 12.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan and EU Discuss Ways to Deepen Cooperation
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's Deputy Foreign Minister Meder Abakirov met with EU representatives in Brussels. They emphasized the importance of maintaining active political dialogue and discussed future bilateral events and high-level visits. Both sides expressed interest in continuing regular dialogue and further developing the partnership between Kyrgyzstan and the European Union.

item.title: Kazakhstan Aims to Boost Domestic Construction Materials to 80% Market Share
item.description: Kazakhstan plans to attract investment for new domestic construction material production facilities. The goal is to increase the share of local materials in the internal market to 80% within three years. Measures will be taken to prevent the unjustified replacement of domestic products with imported ones in construction projects.

item.title: Kazakhstan Plans to Reduce Mortgage Down Payment to 10%
item.description: Kazakhstan is considering lowering the initial mortgage down payment for 'Otbasbank' programs to 10%. The Ministry of Industry and Construction is working on the mechanisms, with new proposals expected around 2027. High demand for programs like 'Umai' indicates a strong need for housing, prompting the development of improved tools.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Considers Tourist Deposits for Mountain Rescue Costs
item.description: Kyrgyzstan is exploring the introduction of deposits for tourists visiting high-mountain routes. These funds could cover state expenses for search and rescue operations in emergencies. The Minister of Emergency Situations stated this, noting that insurance covered a recent helicopter crash during a rescue.

item.title: Uch-Korgon HPP Renovation to Conclude by End of November
item.description: The complete renovation of the Uch-Korgon Hydroelectric Power Plant (HPP) will be finished by the end of November, according to the First Deputy Minister of Energy. Testing of the final aggregate is underway, and the HPP will be fully operational soon. This is part of broader efforts to modernize the country's energy infrastructure.

item.title: Uzbekistan's Population Reaches Over 39 Million, Growing by 9.8 Million in 16 Years
item.description: Uzbekistan's permanent population reached 39,023,600 as of January 1, 2026. This marks an increase of 9,807,700 people, or approximately 33.6%, over the past 16 years since early 2010. In the last year alone, the population grew by 702,000 people, reaching 38,321,600 by the start of 2025.

item.title: Kazakhstan Plans 15 New Production Facilities for Oil and Gas Sector
item.description: Kazakhstan plans to establish 15 new production facilities for the oil and gas industry, with a total project cost of 37.7 billion tenge. Energy Minister Yerlan Akkenzhenov announced that these projects, implemented jointly with global and domestic producers, aim to localize demand for essential goods, create jobs, and develop local manufacturing capabilities.

item.title: Driver Dies After Collision Between Fire Truck and Toyota in Almaty
item.description: A driver has died following a traffic accident in Almaty where a fire truck collided with a Toyota Camry. The incident occurred early on November 17th at the intersection of Auezov and Timiryazev streets. The fire truck was reportedly responding to an emergency with lights and sirens activated.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Brick Factory Fined for Air Pollution Violations
item.description: A brick-producing company in the Sasyk-Bulak village of Kyrgyzstan's Suzak district has been fined 28,000 Kyrgyz soms for violating air protection requirements. An inspection found that the factory's chimneys lacked dust and gas cleaning equipment. The company has been given one month to rectify the deficiencies.

item.title: New International Passenger Train Service Between Tashkent and Astrakhan to Launch December 17
item.description: A new international passenger train service, route number 149/150, will commence operations between Tashkent and Astrakhan starting December 17, 2026. The train will run weekly, departing Tashkent every Thursday and arriving in Astrakhan on Saturdays. The return journey from Astrakhan to Tashkent begins December 20, arriving on Tuesdays. Tickets can be purchased 45 days in advance.

item.title: Kazakhstan to Begin Production of HOWO, Volvo, and Potentially Mercedes Trucks
item.description: Kazakhstan is set to commence the production of HOWO and Sinotruk trucks at the Saran Machinery plant, with Volvo truck tractor production starting in Almaty. Negotiations are also underway for Mercedes truck manufacturing. This initiative aims to develop the country's logistics potential and modernize its vehicle fleet.

item.title: US Vice President Vance: Washington Will Not Allow Iran Conflict to Last Two Years
item.description: US Vice President J.D. Vance stated that the US administration does not intend to allow a war with Iran to drag on for two years or more. He emphasized Washington's commitment to avoiding prolonged military conflicts, while acknowledging the threat posed by Iran's nuclear program. Vance assured that the US would not remain in the region indefinitely.

item.title: Osh, Kyrgyzstan: 10.22 Hectares of Irrigated Farmland Reclassified for Development
item.description: The Kyrgyz government has approved the reclassification of 10.22 hectares of irrigated farmland in Osh for urban development. The land will be used for administrative buildings, multi-story housing, and a public service center. This decision follows a request from the Osh mayor's office and aims to facilitate urban expansion.

item.title: Kazakhstan Fines Exceed 8.2 Million Tenge for Selling Antibiotics Without Prescription
item.description: Kazakhstan has issued 38 protocols for selling antibiotics without a prescription since the start of 2026, with fines totaling over 8.2 million tenge. The Ministry of Health reported that common antibiotics like azithromycin and ceftriaxone are frequently sold without prescriptions. The ministry warned that improper antibiotic use can lead to drug resistance, making treatments less effective.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan and Japan to Cooperate on Kurpsai Hydropower Plant Monitoring System Upgrade
item.description: Kyrgyzstan and the Japan International Cooperation Agency (JICA) are continuing their collaboration on a project to prepare for the rehabilitation of the Kurpsai Hydropower Plant's monitoring and management system. Representatives from "Electric Stations" OJSC met with JICA to discuss project preparation, necessary research, and future joint efforts. Both parties expressed interest in continuing dialogue to enhance the plant's reliability and safety.

item.title: Kazakhstan's Oil Producers to Earn Trillions on Domestic Contracts
item.description: Kazakhstan's oil companies are set to procure goods and services worth 1.595 trillion tenge from domestic producers in 2025, an increase from the previous year. Contracts totaling 301.5 billion tenge have been signed with local manufacturers for 2026.

item.title: Trade Between Kyrgyzstan and Krasnodar Krai Grows 26 Percent
item.description: Trade turnover between Kyrgyzstan and Russia's Krasnodar Krai increased by approximately 26 percent in the first half of the year. Kyrgyzstan primarily imports ferrous metals, fruits, nuts, and plastics from the region.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Ratifies Agreement with Japan for Road Equipment Grant
item.description: Kyrgyzstan has ratified an agreement with Japan for a grant of 533 million yen (approximately $4 million) to purchase five units of road construction machinery. The agreement, signed in August, aims to support the country's economic and social development. The grant will fund the acquisition of specialized equipment, including a road milling machine and various rollers.

item.title: 302 People Died in Kyrgyzstan from Various Incidents Since Start of Year
item.description: Since the beginning of the year, 302 people have died in Kyrgyzstan as a result of 3,649 various incidents. The Minister of Emergency Situations reported a decrease in overall incidents but an increase in fatalities compared to the previous year. Material damage from registered incidents amounted to 1.269 billion soms.

item.title: Kazakhstan Increases Agricultural Support to 1.2 Trillion Tenge
item.description: Government support for farmers in Kazakhstan has grown to 1.2 trillion tenge. This increase aims to bolster the agricultural sector and provide financial assistance to those working in it.

item.title: Uzbekistan Reports 278.3 Billion Sums in Cybercrime Losses Over 10 Months
item.description: From January 1 to October 1, 2026, cybercriminals caused 278.3 billion sums in material damage to citizens in Uzbekistan. The largest losses were due to malware on mobile devices, followed by unauthorized bank card transactions.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Transfers Institute of Balneology to Presidential Affairs Administration
item.description: The Kyrgyz Cabinet has decided to transfer the Kyrgyz Scientific Research Institute of Balneology and Restorative Treatment from the Ministry of Health to the Presidential Affairs Administration. The transfer aims to improve state institution management and optimize state property use. The institute will retain its current staffing, salary conditions, and material base.

item.title: Mudslide Incidents in Kyrgyzstan Increase More Than Fourfold, Minister Reports
item.description: The number of mudslide incidents in Kyrgyzstan has risen more than fourfold, according to the head of the Ministry of Emergency Situations, Kanatbek Chynybaev. In 2026, 355 such cases were registered, resulting in eight deaths, compared to 83 incidents with no fatalities in the previous year. Material damage also significantly increased.

item.title: Uzbekistan Central Bank Head: Need to Increase Confidence in Som, Reduce Dollarization
item.description: Uzbekistan's Central Bank Chairman Timur Ishmetov emphasized the need to reduce the economy's dependence on foreign currency and boost confidence in the national currency, the Som. This is crucial for achieving long-term economic goals, ensuring price stability, and mitigating risks associated with foreign currency fluctuations.

item.title: Eldik Bank Receives SDG Champions 2026 Award for Sustainable Development Contributions
item.description: Eldik Bank has been honored with the SDG Champions 2026 award for its contributions to sustainable development and ESG principles. The award ceremony took place in Almaty during the SDG Forum Almaty 2026. The bank also participated in a panel discussion on transforming SMEs and sustainable supply chains, sharing its experience in supporting entrepreneurship and implementing ESG initiatives.

item.title: Switzerland: Stability in Afghanistan Benefits the Entire Region, Envoy States
item.description: Switzerland's Ambassador to Pakistan, Stéphane Rey, emphasized that stability in Afghanistan is crucial for the entire region. During a meeting with UK and Norwegian envoys, they discussed the current situation and its regional impact. Rey stressed the need for sustained international engagement, close coordination among partners, and continued dialogue with regional countries to ensure Afghanistan's stability.

item.title: Kazakhstan to Offer 15 Pension Fund Investment Portfolio Options
item.description: Kazakhstan is set to introduce 15 investment portfolio options for managing pension savings. Five private management companies will each offer three distinct strategies: conservative, balanced, and aggressive. The Unified Pension Savings Fund (UPSF) will continue to maintain records and provide transparent information on company performance, while the National Bank will manage the main portion of pension assets.

item.title: Mongolian President Resigns Amid Bribery Allegations Linked to Rail Project
item.description: Mongolia's President, Ukhnaagiin Khurelsukh, has announced his resignation following accusations of financial gain from a state railway project. The opposition had demanded the declassification of National Security Council recommendations and the creation of a commission to investigate alleged bribes totaling $110 million related to the Tavan-Tolgoi - Gashuunsuhait railway construction. Khurelsukh stated he will cooperate with the investigation.

item.title: Uber Reports Data Breach Affecting Nearly 150,000 Drivers
item.description: Uber has reported that personal data of approximately 150,000 drivers was stolen due to a cyberattack on its technology partner, Fireworks AI, in October. Hackers gained unauthorized access to Fireworks' systems and subsequently accessed Uber's data, which included driver names, addresses, birth dates, and license numbers.

item.title: Iranian and Omani Foreign Ministers Meet in Muscat to Discuss Regional Challenges
item.description: Iran's Foreign Minister, Abbas Araghchi, met with his Omani counterpart, Badr Al-Busaidi, in Muscat. The two discussed bilateral relations and regional challenges, emphasizing continued dialogue to de-escalate tensions and achieve peaceful solutions. Oman has played a role in indirect negotiations between Iran and the US.

item.title: Kazakhstan Expands Domestic Auto Component Production, Including Engine Blocks
item.description: Kazakhstan is expanding its domestic production of auto components, including engine blocks for trucks. The country already produces batteries, tires, multimedia systems, and seats. Efforts are also underway to increase copper processing and build new smelters, aiming to develop local value chains and utilize more raw materials domestically.

item.title: UN-Habitat Repairs Shelters for Returnee Families in Kunduz and Baghlan
item.description: UN-Habitat is repairing shelters for vulnerable returnee families in Afghanistan's Kunduz and Baghlan provinces, with financial support from the UN Special Trust Fund for Afghanistan. The agency noted a widespread need for shelter and insufficient resources, stressing the necessity for further action to support these families.

item.title: Kazakhstan Aims to Boost Domestic Construction Materials to 80% Market Share
item.description: Kazakhstan plans to increase the share of domestic construction materials in its market to 80% within three years. The registry of Kazakh manufacturers will be integrated with digital systems in the construction sector to support this goal. The ministry aims to ensure local materials are not replaced by imports without valid reasons.
